decisions.reason: As a newly launched supplement range with its own page, A fits the firm's stated consumer-health portfolio expansion and the recent investment and public presentation make management likely to continue rather than reverse course after only one year.

B was launched visibly as a new pharmacy product on its own page, builds on the established offer, and under an escalation-of-commitment logic management would justify the launch by giving it more time in the market.

C supports the firm's broadening of its consumer-health portfolio, has already been publicly introduced as a new product, and there is too little time and too little negative evidence by 2019 for management to withdraw it.

Although less prominently presented, D still builds on the established offer and the firm's expansion strategy, so management is likely to retain it and attribute any early weakness to temporary market-development factors.

Despite the 2018 problem notice, E is a regulated generic medicine that likely required meaningful development, quality, and market-access investment, and management would be inclined to treat the setback as temporary rather than abandon a strategically relevant prescription product so soon.
